topic: K1 prove stable basin-mixed normality for bounded adaptive IPW-Z scores under a finite tail attractor and uniform attraction modulus. K2 prove realized-QV studentization uniformly pivotal. K3 prove a deterministic sandwich valid for a contrast at every nominal level iff its variance is basin-invariant. K4 prove validity for all contrasts iff V_J is deterministic. Include the Guo-Xu two-basin witness and HeartSteps consumer.

open_problems.open_problem: Under what uniform attraction and Cesaro policy-error modulus does a bounded adaptive IPW-Z estimator driven by a recursion with finitely many attained attractors converge stably to a basin-indexed Gaussian law with random covariance V_J?

source_refs.claim: Section 3.1 gives a clipped-LinUCB example with bounded inverse weights, two self-reinforcing fixed points, and a non-Gaussian IPW-Z mixture, while the positive theorem assumes inverse-propensity stabilization.
source_refs.author: Yongyi Guo and Ziping Xu

source_refs.claim: For stochastic approximation with finitely many possible limit points, Borkar bounds the probability of convergence to a prescribed point from its domain of attraction.
source_refs.author: Vivek S. Borkar

source_refs.claim: Stable convergence strengthens weak convergence and supports martingale limits whose Gaussian innovation retains conditioning information.
source_refs.author: David J. Aldous and Geoffrey K. Eagleson

source_refs.excerpt: its predictable quadratic variation converges to one in probability
adaptive-trajectory mixture are left to the solver.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Guo and Xu prove ordinary asymptotic normality only after inverse propensities stabilize; their two-mode clipped-LinUCB witness is numerical and stops at the observation that unstable conditional variance produces a non-Gaussian mixture. The reusable prior martingale lemma likewise assumes predictable QV converges to the deterministic constant one. Stable martingale theory permits random limiting QV and lock-in theory controls convergence after entering an attraction domain, but neither derives Q_T/T → V_J from the exact adaptive IPW recursion uniformly across basins. The first changed proof step is a conditional characteristic-function recursion tested jointly against basin-measurable variables, driven by one attraction/Cesaro modulus that also controls score linearization and inverse-Hessian error.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem uniform over a falsifiable finite-attractor class showing Q_T/T → V_J in probability and (T^(-1/2)S_T, J, Q_T/T) converges stably to (V_J^(1/2)Z, J, V_J), with Z standard Gaussian independent of the basin sigma-field and an explicit attraction-modulus remainder.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from misspecified adaptive deployment to policy instability, the explicit clipped-LinUCB witness, and the inferential consequence.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Misspecified reward models feed back into adaptive assignment -> clipped LinUCB can settle near either of two self-reinforcing limits -> deterministic-variance normal inference fails -> characterize the correct basin-mixed stable limit.

method_exemplars.technique: Use stable convergence for martingale arrays to preserve the basin sigma-field while adjoining an independent Gaussian innovation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired limit is conditionally Gaussian given J rather than an ordinary Gaussian with deterministic covariance.

method_exemplars.technique: Turn attraction-domain lock-in bounds into quantitative tails for post-entry policy error and occupation time.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The basin label and time outside an attractor neighborhood determine whether the Cesaro QV error vanishes.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply bounded-increment martingale normal-approximation bounds that expose normalized quadratic-variation error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A quantitative QV-to-Gaussian bound is the bridge from a uniform attraction modulus to uniform approximation.

open_problems.open_problem: Does same-path realized-quadratic-variation studentization yield a uniformly standard-normal pivot for bounded IPW-Z scores over a finite-attractor adaptive-recursion class, including parameter sequences approaching a basin separatrix?

source_refs.claim: Saco proves pointwise fixed-horizon N(0,1) validity using realized QV without deterministic variance stabilization, under abstract overlap, moment, predictability, and variance-growth assumptions.
source_refs.author: Gabriel Saco

source_refs.claim: The Guo-Xu clipped-LinUCB witness has bounded propensities but two policy modes and unstable conditional score variance.
source_refs.author: Yongyi Guo and Ziping Xu

source_refs.excerpt: No first-order equivalence for the self-normalized variant is asserted.
its predictable quadratic variation converges to one in probability

open_problems.why_unsolved: The generic pointwise claim is occupied by Saco, while the prior CausalSmith work explicitly left first-order equivalence of a self-normalized variant unproved. The live boundary is uniform verification for an endogenous finite-attractor recursion: Saco assumes the moment and variance-ratio conditions rather than deriving them from the recursion, and Guo-Xu provide no realized-versus-predictable QV comparison near the separatrix. The first changed proof step is a uniform matrix martingale bound for realized minus predictable QV, coupled to a lower-tail eigenvalue bound; basin-switching paths can delay variance growth even when every attained basin has positive limiting variance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform self-normalized CLT with sup_P sup_z |P_P(cᵀS_T/sqrt(cᵀ[S]_Tc) ≤ z) - Φ(z)| → 0 for every admissible nonzero contrast c, together with uniform convergence of cᵀ[S]_Tc / cᵀ<S>_Tc to one and a lower-tail bound for the smallest eigenvalue of realized QV.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its contrast between replication-random predictable variance and same-path realized-QV studentization while locating the new work in uniform recursive verification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive assignments leave predictable variance random -> fixed long-run variance can miscalibrate -> realized QV follows the actual path -> prove the pivot uniformly for finite-attractor recursions and near-separatrix sequences.

method_exemplars.technique: Port the realized-QV martingale studentization proof, including the realized-to-predictable variance ratio and feasible plug-in studentizer.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves the exact pointwise pivot that the resolution must upgrade to a uniform recursion-level theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use exponential-supermartingale and pseudo-maximization bounds for martingales normalized by their own sums of squares.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These bounds can control lower-QV and tail events without replacing pathwise scale by a deterministic variance.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert uniform bounded-score and QV approximation errors into a quantitative Gaussian-approximation bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniform pivotality requires an error bound rather than only pointwise convergence.

open_problems.open_problem: For a finite basin-indexed centered Gaussian limit, when is a deterministic sandwich Wald statistic valid at every nominal level for one contrast, and when is one deterministic sandwich valid for all contrasts?

source_refs.claim: Directional stability is target-specific and strictly weaker than target-agnostic stability; it stabilizes predictable QV only in the direction of a scalar target.
source_refs.author: Zikai Shen, Houssam Zenati, Nathan Kallus, Arthur Gretton, Koulik Khamaru, and Aurélien Bibaut

source_refs.claim: Saco notes that one deterministic long-run variance can be conditionally miscalibrated when predictable QV remains random.
source_refs.author: Gabriel Saco

source_refs.claim: Teicher establishes identifiability of finite normal mixtures, supplying the law-identification tool needed for necessity.
source_refs.author: Henry Teicher

source_refs.excerpt: studentized statistics are equivalent exactly when their covariance-kernel projection indices have the same limit.
the variance-rule linearization assumes the main frontier object

open_problems.why_unsolved: Recent adaptive-inference work gives sufficiency under directional or matrix QV stabilization and warns that fixed-variance Wald reporting can fail under random regimes, but it does not state the exact converse. The earlier CausalSmith iff frontier was downgraded because its decisive variance residual was assumed rather than derived. Here finite-normal-mixture identification can derive necessity, but it must be connected to every nominal level and positive basin masses; an isolated level can have accidental correct coverage. The contrastwise claim is strictly weaker than the matrixwise claim because distinct covariance matrices may agree on cᵀV_Jc for one c, whereas agreement for every c must be converted to V_J = S by polarization.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An iff theorem showing that deterministic-S Wald coverage is correct for every α in (0,1) for contrast c exactly when cᵀV_jc = cᵀSc for every positive-mass basin j, and that this holds for every contrast exactly when V_j = S for every such j, plus a witness of accidental correctness at one isolated nominal level.

writing_exemplar.why: Its target-specific-versus-target-agnostic stability distinction frames the separation between one-contrast and all-contrast validity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Scalar causal targets use one covariance direction -> directional stability can hold without matrix stability -> basin covariances may agree for some contrasts but not others -> characterize deterministic-sandwich validity contrastwise and matrixwise.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply finite-normal-mixture identifiability, equivalently uniqueness of the Laplace transform of the variance-mixing law, to prove necessity from equality of the full standardized law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every-level Wald validity identifies the entire absolute centered-Gaussian distribution and should force projected variance mixing to collapse.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the conditional second-moment decomposition to contrast fixed deterministic normalization with realized pathwise normalization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the inferential setup in which random variance regimes translate into conditional Wald miscalibration.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the normal-scale-mixture representation to reduce the coverage question to the mixing distribution.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A basin-indexed scalar limit is exactly a finite centered normal scale mixture.

open_problems.open_problem: What shrinking margin from the separatrix is necessary and sufficient for uniform basin-mixed or realized-QV-studentized inference in the Guo-Xu no-intercept clipped-LinUCB recursion?

source_refs.claim: The no-intercept misspecification creates feedback between arm-specific context proportions and slopes, with two self-reinforcing fixed points selected by early randomness.
source_refs.author: Yongyi Guo and Ziping Xu

source_refs.claim: Borkar's lock-in bound is conditional on being inside a prescribed attraction domain and does not itself give uniform control as the starting point approaches its boundary.
source_refs.author: Vivek S. Borkar

source_refs.claim: Under omnidirectional noise, stochastic approximation avoids unstable critical points, but this is not a quantitative escape-time bound from shrinking neighborhoods.
source_refs.author: Robin Pemantle

source_refs.excerpt: Define one law-independent sequential algorithm class as measurable assignment kernels q_t(a | x, h)
adaptive-trajectory mixture are left to the solver.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Avoidance of an unstable equilibrium is weaker than uniform escape from a shrinking neighborhood, and lock-in bounds valid well inside a basin may degenerate at its boundary. Guo-Xu do not locate the separatrix analytically or bound delayed basin selection in their exact recursion. The prior sequential-design review also requires an explicit history-measurable assignment kernel before law-dependent claims can be made. Thus the first proof step is a uniform hitting-time and occupation bound for starts whose separatrix distance may shrink with T; without it, neither predictable-QV convergence nor realized-QV lower-tail control is uniform.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp frontier giving a rate δ_T such that starts at distance at least δ_T from the separatrix obey uniform attraction, occupation, QV, inverse-QV, and Gaussian-approximation bounds, while a concrete smaller-order approaching-separatrix sequence retains nonvanishing delayed-lock-in probability and proves that global inference must be margin-restricted.

writing_exemplar.why: Keep its concrete no-intercept two-context recursion and inferential pathology as the running witness rather than discussing separatrices abstractly.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Model misspecification creates two stable policy modes -> early noise chooses a basin -> starts near the separating set delay or randomize that choice -> determine whether unrestricted uniform inference is possible or requires a margin.

method_exemplars.technique: Make the lock-in probability bound explicit as a function of entrance time and distance to an attractor neighborhood.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniform inferential error depends on a uniform tail bound for the time at which the policy becomes basin-local.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt unstable-point nonconvergence into an exit-time or anti-concentration bound near the separating equilibrium.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The separatrix is organized by an unstable point that paths avoid asymptotically but may shadow for inference-relevant durations.

method_exemplars.technique: Feed attraction and QV error rates into a bounded-increment martingale Gaussian-approximation inequality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This converts a dynamical margin rate into an explicit uniform coverage error.

open_problems.open_problem: Can basin-mixed stable limits and realized-QV pivots be established for causal-excursion-effect WCLS/IPW-Z estimators in pooled HeartSteps-type micro-randomized trials whose online assignment algorithm has finitely many random attractors?

source_refs.claim: The paper defines causal excursion effects, reviews WCLS inference, and uses HeartSteps to illustrate repeated within-person sequential randomization.
source_refs.author: Tianchen Qian, Ashley E. Walton, Linda M. Collins, Predrag Klasnja, Stephanie T. Lanza, Inbal Nahum-Shani, Mashfiqui Rabbi, Michael A. Russell, Maureen A. Walton, Hyesun Yoo, and Susan A. Murphy

source_refs.claim: The HeartSteps online reinforcement-learning algorithm uses randomized actions to choose activity suggestions five times daily.
source_refs.author: Peng Liao, Kristjan Greenewald, Predrag Klasnja, and Susan A. Murphy
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies

source_refs.claim: The paper develops adaptive-sandwich Z-estimation for pooled longitudinal trajectories but uses fixed within-user horizon and a diverging number of users.
source_refs.author: Kelly W. Zhang, Lucas Janson, and Susan A. Murphy

source_refs.claim: Guo and Xu analyze growing-horizon IPW-Z inference with i.i.d. arrivals and include a HeartSteps V1-calibrated application, but require stability for their Gaussian theorem.
source_refs.author: Yongyi Guo and Ziping Xu

open_problems.why_unsolved: The relevant literatures use incompatible asymptotic and dependence regimes. Standard MRT theory permits endogenous within-person histories but usually treats the randomization schedule as designed and stable; pooled adaptive-longitudinal theory sends the number of users to infinity with fixed decision horizon; Guo-Xu's growing-horizon theory assumes i.i.d. arrivals and a convergent policy. A HeartSteps consumer must handle cluster martingale scores, assignment feedback shared across participants, availability, and a causal excursion estimand. The first changed proof step is the martingale linearization and QV decomposition, which must separate within-person serial terms, cross-user dependence induced by the pooled learner, and the basin variable.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint-(n,T) stable CLT for a prespecified HeartSteps causal excursion contrast with basin-indexed cluster covariance, accompanied by a feasible cluster realized-QV studentizer whose Wald statistic is uniformly N(0,1) under quantitative attraction, availability, overlap, and within-person dependence conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: Adopt its application-native progression from JITAI decisions to causal excursion effects, repeated randomization, and HeartSteps analysis.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: JITAIs make repeated context-dependent treatment decisions -> MRTs identify causal excursions from the treatment schedule -> an online learner makes that schedule path-dependent and potentially basin-random -> develop valid excursion-effect inference under finite-attractor adaptation.

method_exemplars.technique: Port the adaptive sandwich and non-i.i.d. empirical-process decomposition for pooled longitudinal Z-estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It handles cross-user dependence and repeated measures missing from the single-stream Guo-Xu setup.

method_exemplars.technique: Use IPW-Z to retain marginal-target consistency under reward-model misspecification, then replace deterministic policy convergence by finite-attractor stable-QV convergence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is a Z-estimand under adaptive assignment, retaining Guo-Xu's misspecification and basin mechanism.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt same-path realized-QV studentization after deriving the appropriate cluster martingale score.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the limit-theory move that can remove random basin covariance once the HeartSteps score is a martingale array.

literature_map:
Guo and Xu (2026, arXiv:2606.22639) is the closest anchor: its clipped-LinUCB/no-intercept witness has bounded inverse weights, two self-reinforcing policy limits, and a non-Gaussian IPW-Z mixture.
Its positive IPW-Z theorem instead assumes scaled inverse-propensity convergence and delivers ordinary Gaussian limits with a consistent sandwich, leaving finite random attractors untreated.
Saco (2026, arXiv:2602.15559) already proves the generic pointwise fixed-horizon realized-QV Studentized pivot without deterministic variance stabilization; K2 is live only as a uniform recursive/separatrix result.
Shen et al. (2026, arXiv:2602.21478) distinguish scalar directional stability from target-agnostic matrix stability and prove efficient normal inference when the relevant predictable-QV direction stabilizes.
Leiner, Dunn, and Ramdas (2025/2026, arXiv:2509.14218) permit unstable policies by estimating time-varying score covariance, but do not characterize basin-mixed limits or same-path finite-attractor uniformity.
Hadad et al. (2021, PNAS, arXiv:1911.02768) and Bibaut et al. (2021, NeurIPS, arXiv:2106.00418) stabilize adaptive AIPW/DR scores by reweighting conditional variances.
Zhang, Janson, and Murphy (2020, NeurIPS, arXiv:2002.03217) show standard bandit OLS can be nonnormal and construct a batched-normal alternative.
Chen, Lu, and Song (2021, JASA, arXiv:2010.07283) prove IPW inference for epsilon-greedy contextual bandits and use a margin condition near the decision boundary.
Zhang, Janson, and Murphy (2022, arXiv:2202.07098) develop adaptive-sandwich Z-estimation for pooled longitudinal data in the fixed-T, growing-n regime.
Borkar (2002) gives attractor lock-in probabilities, while Pemantle (1990) proves avoidance of unstable equilibria; neither supplies uniform escape-time control near a separatrix.
Aldous and Eagleson (1978) provide stable-convergence machinery for conditionally Gaussian martingale limits, and Mourrat (2013, arXiv:1103.5050) quantifies bounded-increment martingale CLT error through QV error.
Teicher (1963) identifies finite normal mixtures, and Andrews and Mallows (1974) characterize normal scale mixtures; together they support necessity in the deterministic-sandwich frontier.
Qian et al. (2022, Psychological Methods, arXiv:2107.03544), Liao et al. (2020, IMWUT, arXiv:1909.03539), and Boruvka et al. (2018, JASA, arXiv:1601.00237) anchor the HeartSteps/MRT consumer and causal-excursion estimand.
The unoccupied intersection is a uniform finite-attractor recursion theorem joining basin lock-in, stable martingale limits, realized-QV studentization, contrastwise-versus-matrixwise variance invariance, and HeartSteps-type longitudinal scores.
prior_proposal_map:
No upgrade parent was supplied. The current exp_bandit_random_qv_studentization_frontier directory contains only state.json, pipeline.jsonl, and orchestrator/decision_log.jsonl; it had no proposal core, rejected angle, review JSON, README, or writeup to mine.
A bounded catalogue-wide scan covered 111 proto_core files, 1,389 review JSONs, 170 bank READMEs, 73 discovery/writeup.tex files, and 198 rejected-angle artifacts, then narrowed to adaptive/bandit/martingale/QV/studentization terms.
stat_transport_boundary_overlap_calibration_frontier_v1 supplied the deterministic-predictable-QV martingale-array CLT and local Hall-Heyde/self-normalization pointers.
stat_sequential_second_order_frontier_v1 supplied the unresolved adaptive-trajectory mixture and reviewer insistence on explicit history-measurable assignment kernels; angle0_v1-v3 and the general, math, and rubric reviews were inspected.
exp_crossworld_robust_controlvariate_design_v1 supplied the explicit limitation that first-order equivalence of its self-normalized implementation was not established; its angle0_v1-v3 reviews were inspected.
eid_dml_orth_uniform_v1 supplied the closest prior iff studentization frontier and the decisive reviewer failure that variance-rule geometry was assumed rather than derived; its final proposal, two rejected-angle proposals, README, and angle0/1/2 reviewer series were inspected.
stat_neyman_regret_minimax_v1 supplied adaptive HT/AIPW comparators and Cook-Mishler-Ramdas/Kato adaptive-inference pointers; its README, proposal core, writeup, and reviews were inspected.
No prior proposal/reviewer/README/writeup match for HeartSteps, Guo-Xu, finite tail attractors, the two-basin recursion, basin-mixed normality, or separatrix uniformity was found; the four linked prior entries are technique-derived directions rather than claims that a prior proposal posed the destination problem.
